text: A procedure tells one person the steps for one task. A workflow is the bigger picture — the full path a request takes across different people until it's actually resolved.

Almost every governance workflow shares the same backbone: intake, where the request enters; triage, sorting what it is and how urgent; routing, getting it to the right person using the RACI matrix; resolution, the actual fix; verification, confirming it actually worked; and closure, recording what happened.

An access request routes to the data owner for approval and IT provisions it. A data quality issue gets triaged by severity and routed to a steward for a fix. A policy exception request needs a business reason, a time-bound scope, committee approval, and an expiration date so it doesn't quietly become permanent.

Many programs run these through a ticketing system or a data catalog's workflow feature, or even a spreadsheet for a small program. But the tool is just delivery — a well-configured tool running an undefined process just produces fast, untracked chaos. Design the stages and the accountability first.
Next lesson: what happens when a workflow's resolution stage gets stuck — issue management and escalation.
